summary: These tables cover activity at Title IV postsecondary institutions during July 1, 2008–June 30, 2009, using institution-level records for the full 12-month reporting period. The survey includes institutions eligible and required to report IPEDS data, with enrollment reported separately for undergraduate and graduate levels where applicable; it is intended to capture institutions operating nontraditional calendars or short-term programs as well as conventional institutions. The 12-month measures describe the institution’s activity over the entire period rather than enrollment at a single point in time.

This Completions survey counts awards conferred by eligible IPEDS postsecondary institutions during the July 1–June 30 reporting year; the unit is an institution-level award count rather than an individual student record. The universe covers institutions awarding postsecondary certificates or degrees. For 2008–09, the second year of a three-year transition, institutions could report using old race/ethnicity categories, new categories, or a combination; the files therefore include race/ethnicity measures reflecting both reporting systems and derived combined categories.

Fall Enrollment reports institution-level student counts for the fall reporting period. Traditional-calendar institutions report enrollment as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with differing or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. Tables may contain multiple records per institution, and the survey covers institutions included and eligible for IPEDS fall-enrollment reporting.

Finance is an annual collection of institution-level financial activity for the covered fiscal year, including revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities under the institution’s applicable accounting standards. Its universe is postsecondary institutions in the IPEDS reporting universe that are required or eligible to submit finance data; the unit of observation is the institution’s fiscal-year record, not an individual student or program. Reporting is organized by accounting basis, with separate forms for GASB, FASB, and private for-profit institutions.

This survey reports outcomes through August 31, 2009 for cohorts of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at IPEDS-reporting institutions with eligible undergraduate programs. Institutions report cohort enrollment and subsequent completion or transfer status at defined percentages of normal time, with cohort years and outcome windows varying by institution level. The survey covers four-year, two-year, and less-than-two-year institutions, with some measures applying only to particular institution types.

Human Resources covers staff on institutional payroll as of November 1, 2009, plus salary and fringe-benefit reporting for the 2009-10 academic year. The unit is the institution, with multiple records per institution identified by table-specific occupational, rank, contract, or benefit dimensions; eligibility varies by table, and related administrative offices may also report. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2009 (odd) has data, and 2009 was still in the transition to new race/ethnicity categories, with old, new, and derived categories available where applicable.

These institution-level tables cover the 2009-10 academic year for institutions in the 2009-10 IPEDS universe. Active institutions participating in Title IV federal financial aid programs are required to report to IPEDS; the tables include institutional characteristics, reporting status, charges, and mission information. Some content is conditional on institutional structure or program type, such as admissions data for non-open-admission institutions and charges reported according to the institution’s academic or vocational calendar.

This annual survey reports institution-level undergraduate student financial aid for the academic year from July 1, 2008, through June 30, 2009, at postsecondary institutions participating in IPEDS/Title IV reporting. Its universe is undergraduate students receiving aid, with reporting centered on full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking students and, for some measures, all undergraduates. The survey covers aid amounts and sources and includes net-price reporting for eligible first-time undergraduate groups.
